segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle,
an electric bicycle
or an electric scooter
shall not: Overtake and pass a motor vehicle
unless the operator can do so safely without endangering himself or herself or the occupants of the motor vehicle.

elements.justification: 'bicycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride, having two tandem wheels ... except a moped'); claimed as the aggregate, never expanded into classes. 'The operator of' names who controls the device, read through the device's controlled motion (agency reading below), so the aggregate is the subject's class.

'an electric bicycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts'); claimed as the aggregate.
'an electric scooter' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); claimed as the aggregate.

Overtaking and passing is drv.interaction.overtaking(x, y): the two head the same way, are side by side (footprints overlapping along x's heading) and x gains on y; the concept states no side, as the words state none. The overtaken party is 'a motor vehicle', the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'), as the mapping index maps 'The driver of a motor vehicle'. The motor vehicle is quantified in the rule, not a binder: the duty arises only where one is overtaken.

operationalizations.standard: can do so safely without endangering himself or herself or the occupants of the motor vehicle
operationalizations.convention: Endangering the occupants of the motor vehicle and the rider himself or herself is read through the measured clearance of the pass and through predicted conflicts: the lateral component of rel.surface_gap between the rider and the overtaken motor vehicle ('distance between the nearest points of two bodies ... its longitudinal and lateral components') is compared with the lateral clearance of the bicycle operating envelope, so the bound moves with the measured gap; and no other road user stands in a predicted conflict with the rider under the traffic-conflict technique (closest approach within the time horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance), the magnitude of the predicted closest approach entering the bound. A rel.surface_gap is a clearance, not a centre distance, so the side-by-side pass itself is judged on the bodies' gap.

applicability: x is a member of one of the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter that, at the judged observation, overtakes some road user y other than x that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle: drv.interaction.overtaking(x, y) with p.same_direction_cos_tolerance and p.motion_speed_tolerance.
obligation: For every motor vehicle y (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, not x) that x overtakes at the observation: the lateral component of rel.surface_gap between x and y is at least p.overtaking_lateral_clearance, and no road user z other than x and y is in a predicted conflict with x, that is, not both prim.closest_approach_within(x, z) over p.conflict_time_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance(x, z) over that horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Violated where x overtakes a motor vehicle while either bound fails.

narrowings.why: 'The operator of' names who controls the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter; it is read through the device's controlled motion, whoever is at the controls.

Overtaking and passing is judged in its side-by-side phase, where the rider gains on the motor vehicle with the footprints overlapping along the rider's heading; the approach from behind and the moment of drawing clear ahead are not separately judged.

Safety and endangering are read only through the lateral clearance to the overtaken motor vehicle and predicted conflicts of the rider with other road users; other hazards of the manoeuvre (surface, visibility) are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle travels beside a car in the same direction, footprints overlapping along its heading, 2 m/s faster than the car, with the lateral surface gap between them well below the lateral clearance; no other road user is present.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same pass with a lateral surface gap above the lateral clearance and no other road user in predicted conflict.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides alone on the road; no motor vehicle is present, so nothing is overtaken.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: An electric bicycle overtakes a car side by side; the source does not supply surface gaps.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle overtakes a car with an ample lateral gap while a truck approaching head-on is predicted to come within the conflict clearance of the bicycle within the horizon.

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cos_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Heading alignment: cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same way of travel (about a quarter of a right angle).
param_proposals.source: Trajectory-based heading classification of road users.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique and time-to-collision studies (Hayward 1972; Hyden 1987).

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict.
param_proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique; passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO).

param_proposals.name: p.overtaking_lateral_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Lateral clearance of the bicycle operating envelope: the shy distance between a bicyclist's body and a motor vehicle beside it below which the pass is close enough to endanger either.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (bicyclist operating space and shy distance to motor vehicles, about 1 m).

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
A person driving a motorcycle,
moped or trimobile
or riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
facing the signal
may proceed straight through or turn in the direction opposite that indicated by the green turn arrow if:

(1) The person stops before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made or, in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, before entering the intersection;
(2) The person waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows of the applicable official traffic-control device and the signal does not change
because of a malfunction or because the signal failed to detect the presence of the motorcycle, moped, trimobile, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter;
(3) No other device at the place prohibits the turn,
if applicable;
and (4) The person yields the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

elements.justification: The signal is a dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady red with a green turn arrow is circular_red displayed together with green_arrow(left) or green_arrow(right); circular_red is the steady red, flashing_red being a separate state. The signal is the one governing the road user's approach (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'): the carrier of kind st.travel_region the road user occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), or the intersection (st.intersection) itself. Not a stand-in for a position: governance says which device applies, not where to halt. The display is read at the entry into the intersection, the event the words fix it to ('facing the signal may proceed').

'motorcycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels ...'); claimed as the aggregate. 'A person driving' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading).

'moped' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped. 'trimobile' has no applicable definition and no aggregate; the nearest class atom is ru.motorcycle, 'motor vehicle on two or three wheels ridden astride, including three-wheeled variants', which denotes the three-wheeled machines ridden astride; a three-wheeled motor vehicle driven from a seat is not ridden astride and is not denoted, so a gap is recorded for it.

The admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ...') and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor'); each claimed as its aggregate. 'riding' is read through the device's controlled motion.

Facing the signal: the signal governs the approach the road user enters through, the carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) at the observation before its entry whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters), dev.governs naming the carrier, or governing the intersection itself. The road user's heading is not read: st.lane_enters states that the approach is the carrier occupied, 'never ... the road user's velocity or heading'.

Proceeding straight through is drv.motion.straight_through_region(x, i) at x's exit from the intersection; turning in the direction opposite the arrow is drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(x, i) where the green arrow displayed at entry is green_arrow(left), and drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(x, i) where it is green_arrow(right); each concept reads the heading change since entry integrated from kin.yaw_rate over the overlap with the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection). The permission's movement is recognized where the crossing ends, the exit.

'stops' is a required stop, DEF-NRS-484A-255 ('complete cessation from movement'), the concept drv.motion.stopped ('the definition's "complete cessation from movement"'). The place is read on the approach carrier (st.travel_region, rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters): the pavement marking that indicates where the stop must be made is a st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device', recorded as marking that carrier's entrance (st.entrance_of, 'exactly that carrier's entrance'); failing one, the crosswalk on the nearest side, a st.crosswalk the source records as marking that carrier's entrance; failing both, the entrance end of the carrier at the intersection (st.intersection). Whether the halt lies short of the place is read along the carrier's designated direction by prim.region_offset_along and the body-to-mark distance by st.region_geometry, as the ontology's approach convention states. Not a stand-in for distance to the line: the line's association is the source's record.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle, DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped, DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, or carries ru.motorcycle (the trimobile); at the judged observation x leaves an intersection i; at x's entry into i (the observation at which x's overlap with i last became true, read through a past operator) a traffic signal s governing the approach carrier c that x occupied at the observation before the entry (dev.governs(s, c) with st.lane_enters(c, i), or dev.governs(s, i)) displayed circular_red together with green_arrow(dir), dir left or right; and the crossing x completes is a through movement (drv.motion.straight_through_region(x, i)) or a turn opposite the arrow (drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(x, i) where dir is left, drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(x, i) where dir is right), with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph and the angles p.straight_through_max_heading_change, p.left_turn_min_angle, p.right_turn_min_angle, p.reversal_min_angle.
obligation: Trigger: the entry of x into i found by the applicability. Place: on the approach carrier c, the stop line recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of) where one is recorded; else the crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance, on the near side; else c's entrance end at i. Act: x halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance) while on c at the place: within p.stop_point_tolerance of the mark by body distance (st.region_geometry), not beyond it along c's designated direction (sign of prim.region_offset_along), and with its footprint not overlapping the crosswalk (for the crosswalk place) or i (for the intersection place). History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start, the last observation before the entry at which x, on a carrier the mark is recorded as marking, is outside the mark's stopping zone upstream (off the mark, short of it and farther than p.stop_point_tolerance from it), or at x's previous entry into i, whichever is later; nothing else ends it. A halt found: met. Either end reached without a halt: violated. Neither end reached without a halt (the approach began before the recording): unknown. A mark whose entrances are observed and exclude c does not govern, and the next place in the words' order is read; a mark whose association with c is unobserved leaves the place unknown where the verdict depends on it.

narrowings.why: 'A person driving' names who controls the motorcycle, moped or trimobile; read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

The sign or pavement marking that 'indicates where the stop must be made' is read through the stop line the source records as marking the approach's entrance; a sign that indicates a stopping place without a line is not read as a place of its own.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle in an approach lane with a recorded stop line faces circular_red with green_arrow(left) from the approach start onwards, rolls across the stop line without halting, enters the intersection and leaves it with a heading change below the straight-through bound.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same motorcycle halts at the stop line within the stop-point tolerance, later enters and goes straight through.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle enters on circular_red with green_arrow(left) and makes a left turn through the intersection, the movement the arrow indicates.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A moped goes straight through on red with a green left arrow; the source supplies no speed, so whether it halted on the approach is unknown.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with an electric scooter already within the stopping zone of the stop line of its approach; it enters on red with a green right arrow and makes a left turn; no halt is recorded and neither the approach start nor a previous entry lies in the recording.
scenarios.boundary: the approach start upstream of the stop line, which lies before the recording begins

Waiting is staying on the approach without entering the intersection after the halt (drv.motion.stopped, a required stop of DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement') that begins the wait, on the carrier (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) that enters the intersection (st.lane_enters). residues.why: The cause the words name (a malfunction, or a failure to detect the road user) is what a signal's not changing for a waiting road user through two complete cycles consists in; once the obligation reads two complete cycles with no change, the cause adds no further restriction, so the duty is the same whether or not these words are read.

applicability: As NRS_484B_307_9b_o1: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle, DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped, DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, or carries ru.motorcycle; at the judged observation x leaves an intersection i; at x's entry into i (read through a past operator) a traffic signal s governing x's approach carrier c (dev.governs(s, c), st.lane_enters(c, i)) or i displayed circular_red with green_arrow(dir), dir left or right; and the crossing is a through movement or a turn opposite the arrow (drv.motion.straight_through_region, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region under a left arrow, drv.motion.left_turn_through_region under a right arrow).

Violated where x entered with fewer complete arrow cycles in its wait or after s had displayed circular_green during it. Where the wait began before the recording, the count is unknown.

The 'applicable official traffic-control device' is the signal head present and governing the approach; its official status is presumed from its presence.

A complete cycle of the lights or lighted arrows is read as one display of the green turn arrow that lights and goes out within the wait; a cycle of the circular indications without an arrow display is not counted separately.

facing the signal

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'). The law's own qualifier 'vehicular' limits the members the duty reads to those travelling by vehicle or conveyance: it leaves out pedestrians, read by the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian as a condition beside the traffic aggregate (x is not a pedestrian), and ridden or herded animals, which no road-user class of the ontology carries. segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not make a U-turn
in an area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone
except:
(a) When there are no children present;
(b) On a day on which school is not in session;
(c) During the period from a half hour after school is no longer in operation to a half hour before school is next in operation;
(d) If the zone is designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the hours when the pupils of the school are in class
and the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect;
or (e) If the zone is not designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the times when the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect.

As used in this section, “speed limit beacon” means a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit in a school zone or school crossing zone is in effect.

elements.justification: 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), as the mapping index maps 'The driver of a vehicle'. 'The driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080, 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'U-turn' is defined by DEF-NRS-484B-077 ('the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction, whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not'), which the concept drv.motion.u_turn carries with that definition: the heading change over the recognition window within the reversal band, integrated across forward and backing moves.

An area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone is the stretch a dev.zone_sign of kind school or school_crossing ('a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}') posts: the travel regions it governs (dev.governs) that x occupies (rel.occupies) of kind st.travel_region. The definitions (DEF-NRS-484B-063 'those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property', DEF-NRS-484B-060 'those sections of streets ... that pupils cross') describe legal region classes; the ontology reads the sign where the category is also marked on the road. Not a stand-in for whether the posted condition holds now, which prim.conditions_hold reads in exception (e).

Children present are road users of class ru.child ('pedestrian who is visibly a child') whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the highway (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders') that the zone's governed region lies on (st.on_way). Not a stand-in for the roadway: the whole way, sidewalks included, is where children are present in the zone.

A zone designated by a speed limit beacon is one where a dev.speed_limit_beacon ('a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect') governs (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). 'operational' is read as the beacon not being dev.inoperative ('a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication').

The yellow lights not flashing in the manner indicating the limit is in effect is the beacon's flashing attribute false: dev.speed_limit_beacon, 'flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect; flashing attribute'.
The zone is not designated by an operational beacon: no dev.speed_limit_beacon that is not dev.inoperative governs (dev.governs) a travel region x occupies (rel.occupies).

The sign designating the zone is the dev.zone_sign of kind school or school_crossing governing (dev.governs) the region x occupies; its 'conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend — a list of time windows ...' states when its speed limit is in effect, and the limit is not in effect where prim.conditions_hold ('the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user') is false.

The section's definition of a speed limit beacon ('a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately') is what dev.speed_limit_beacon denotes: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'.

assumptions.meaning: The school the zone serves is not in session on the day of the observation.
The observation falls in the period that begins a half hour after the school the zone serves last ceased operation and ends a half hour before it next begins operation.
The pupils of the school the zone serves are in class at the observation.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that makes a U-turn: drv.motion.u_turn(x) rises at the judged observation (window p.turn_recognition_window, angles p.reversal_min_angle and p.reversal_max_angle); at some observation while the U-turn is under way (in the window behind the recognition, where drv.motion.turning(x) with p.yaw_rate_tolerance) x occupies a travel region r governed by a dev.zone_sign z of kind school or school_crossing.
obligation: The U-turn is violated unless at every observation while it is under way (throughout) one of the exceptions holds, the same one at each: (a) no ru.child occupies the highway h that r lies on (st.on_way(r, h)); (b) asm.school_not_in_session; (c) asm.school_out_of_operation_period; (d) a dev.speed_limit_beacon b, not dev.inoperative, governs a travel region x occupies, and asm.pupils_in_class, and b's flashing attribute is false; (e) no such operational beacon governs a travel region x occupies, and prim.conditions_hold(z, x) is false. segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection
and: The turn is a right turn,
both the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane
if the highway has a right turn lane
as set forth in subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 [NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b],
or must be made from the extreme right lane.

elements.justification: 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), as the mapping index maps 'The driver of a vehicle'; 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

The intersection is the region the intention is declared at and the vehicle enters: a st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet'), anchored by the carrier x occupies (rel.occupies) of kind st.travel_region whose entrance end is that intersection (st.lane_enters).

The right turn lane is a st.turn_lane of side right ('a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}'). The approach for the turn is the carrier through which x approaches the intersection, which st.lane_enters defines as 'a carrier it occupies whose entrance end is that intersection'; the turn is made from it when x enters the intersection (rel.occupies of st.intersection rising) out of it. Both are read at the observation before the entry: every carrier x occupies there that enters the intersection is the right turn lane.

The highway has a right turn lane 'as set forth in subsection 4', whose words are 'If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning': a st.turn_lane of side right ('a lane designated only for turning') that is the rightmost lane of its direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane', so ordinal equal to count), lying on (st.on_way) the highway (st.highway) of the carrier x occupies (rel.occupies) and entering the intersection x enters (st.lane_enters, st.intersection). The mapping index maps the borrowed words to rel.occupies, st.highway, st.lane_adjacency, st.on_way, st.turn_lane; st.lane_enters and st.intersection tie the lane to this junction.

compositions.quote: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: Borrows the qualifiers 'single', 'right lane' and 'to be used only for turning', which set forth what the highway's right turn lane is; this duty needs only that such a lane exists, and whether subsection 4's own duty (driving in that lane only to turn right) applies or is complied with decides nothing here.

compositions.quote: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: Borrows the same qualifiers from the same opening words of subsection 4; this duty needs only that such a lane exists, and whether subsection 4's own duty (not travelling through an intersection from that lane) applies or is complied with decides nothing here.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that enters an intersection i at the judged observation (rel.occupies(x, i) rises), with int.turn_right(x, i) declared true at that observation; and the highway has a right turn lane: at the observation before the entry x occupies a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, i), and some st.turn_lane t of side right with st.lane_enters(t, i), lying on the same highway h as c (st.on_way(t, h), st.on_way(c, h)), is the rightmost lane of its direction (st.lane_adjacency ordinal equal to count) and is c or a lane reached from c through right-neighbour links of st.lane_adjacency.
obligation: At the observation before the entry, x occupies such a right turn lane t, and every carrier x occupies there that enters i is a st.turn_lane of side right: the approach for the turn and the turn are made from the right turn lane. Violated where x enters i with its intention to turn right from a carrier entering i that is not the right turn lane.

narrowings.why: The approach for the right turn is read at the observation before the entry, as the carrier through which x approaches the intersection then; how far upstream the approach in the turn lane began is not judged.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

scenarios.name: permit

segmentation.text: A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled
in a business or residential district
and not less than the last 300 feet traveled
in any other area
prior to changing the course
of a vehicle.
This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.

elements.justification: A signal of intention is the signal itself, never a declared intention (the ontology: 'a signal "of intention" is the signal'): sig.turn_indicator ('state ∈ {off, left, right}') or sig.hand_signal ('a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, ...}'), of the side of the turn; not a stand-in for the turn itself, which is judged separately through motion. Turning right or left, or otherwise from a direct course, is the heading departing to that side from the designated direction of the carrier the vehicle occupies: drv.lane.heading_offset_from_direction, the signed departure (left positive) of kin.heading from st.lane_direction, on a carrier of kind st.travel_region x occupies (rel.occupies). 'continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled' is a window in distance travelled (a .path window), which reads kin.path_length ('distance travelled along the body's path'); the figure is the law's literal.
'not less than the last 300 feet traveled' is the same .path window over kin.path_length with the law's other literal, the bound selected outside a business or residence district.

Changing the course is the event at which the heading's departure from the occupied carrier's direction (drv.lane.heading_offset_from_direction over kin.heading and st.lane_direction, on a st.travel_region x occupies) first exceeds the course-change tolerance to a side: the observation at which that condition became true. The signal window lies behind it ('prior to').
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway').

assumptions.meaning: The stretch of highway at the observation lies within territory classed as a business district or as a residence district.

residues.why: The words say the rule holds in every weather; no weather condition restricts or extends the duty, which is the same whether or not it rains, snows or is clear.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that changes course at the judged observation: x occupies a travel region c with a designated direction, and drv.lane.heading_offset_from_direction(x, c) rises above p.course_change_sin_tolerance (a change to the left) or below its negative (a change to the right) at this observation, not having done so at the observation before (rises).
obligation: At that observation, a signal of the side of the change held at every observation of the window of path length x travelled behind it (holdsFor .path): for a change to the left, sig.turn_indicator state left or sig.hand_signal meaning left; for a change to the right, state right or meaning right. The window's length is selected with Term.cond: the literal 100 ft where asm.business_or_residence_district holds, the literal 300 ft where it does not. A window reaching before the start of the trace leaves the verdict unknown.

narrowings.why: Turning right or left and otherwise turning from a direct course are read as the heading departing from the designated direction of the carrier the vehicle occupies; a change of course made where the vehicle occupies no carrier with a designated direction is not judged.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle in a lane with a designated direction, asm.business_or_residence_district declared true, lights sig.turn_indicator left only over the last 10 m of path before its heading departs to the left of the lane direction beyond the tolerance; the trace covers more than 100 ft behind the change.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same vehicle and district, with sig.turn_indicator left lit at every observation of the last 50 m of path before the heading departs to the left.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle drives along its lane with its heading aligned with the lane direction throughout; no change of course occurs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle changes course to the left in its lane in a district; the source observes neither turn indicators nor arm signals.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_or_residence_district declared false; the vehicle signals right over the last 50 m of path (above 100 ft but below 300 ft) before its heading departs to the right of the lane direction.

param_proposals.name: p.course_change_sin_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Lane-change kinematics: the heading of a vehicle changing lanes or turning departs from the lane direction by about three degrees or more, a smaller departure being in-lane steering correction; the bound is the sine of that angle.
param_proposals.source: Naturalistic lane-change trajectory studies (heading-angle distributions of lane changes, e.g. Toledo and Zohar 2007; NGSIM lane-change analyses).

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle,
whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event an unobstructed width of the highway opposite a standing vehicle shall be left
for the free passage of other vehicles
and a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.
This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled
while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway
in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: Upon any highway: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders', as the mapping index maps 'upon any highway'. Not a stand-in for the roadway, which e6 reads.

Stop, when prohibited, is DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; park (DEF-NRS-484A-155, 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of ... loading or unloading') and standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of ... receiving or discharging passengers') are halts too. The halt is drv.motion.stopped (kin.speed at or below its resolution). The stopping definition's exclusion, which the concept's contract does not make, is carried by the rule beside it: a halt necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic (another road user ahead of x in its lane, rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, within the queue standstill gap by rel.surface_gap; or one in a predicted conflict with x, prim.closest_approach_within with prim.closest_approach_distance below the conflict clearance), or one in compliance with an officer's direction (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, indication stop) or a device (a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, a dev.stop_sign or a dev.yield_sign) governing (dev.governs) the travel region x occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). 'no person' is read through the vehicle's conduct (agency reading).
'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), the subject's class.

The paved or main-traveled part of the highway is the st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', lying on that highway (st.on_way); x's footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies). Not a stand-in for the sidewalk: the shoulder and verge are off the roadway, which is where the words direct the vehicle.
While on the paved or main-traveled portion: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the st.roadway ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder') at the observation.

operationalizations.standard: practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway
operationalizations.convention: Practicability of halting off the roadway is read through the space off the roadway beside the vehicle: a st.shoulder lying on the same highway (st.on_way) whose boundary lies within one standard lane width of the vehicle's body (st.region_geometry ground distance from the body outline, compared with the reach), so the distance measured enters the bound, and on which no other halted road user occupies (rel.occupies) the stretch alongside the vehicle (rel.longitudinal_overlap not negative). A shoulder farther than the reach, or one taken alongside, makes halting off the roadway not practicable.

assumptions.meaning: The stretch of highway at the observation lies within territory classed as a business district or as a residence district.
The road user's vehicle cannot be moved from the place where it stands at the observation, by its own power or otherwise.

residues.why: Attended or unattended, the duty is the same: the words name both cases and exclude neither, so no observation of occupancy is read.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle occupying a highway h (rel.occupies, st.highway) and the roadway rw lying on it (st.roadway, st.on_way(rw, h)); asm.business_or_residence_district is false at the observation; and not the exception: not (asm.vehicle_disabled and x occupies a roadway and asm.disabled_vehicle_immovable).
obligation: Violated at an observation where x is halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance), the halt is not excepted, and halting off the roadway is practicable. Excepted halts: some road user z other than x is ahead of x in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with rel.surface_gap below p.queue_standstill_gap, or is in a predicted conflict with x (prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_time_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance); or a device governing a travel region x occupies directs the halt (dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, red_arrow or flashing_red; dev.stop_sign; dev.yield_sign; dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop). Practicable: some st.shoulder s with st.on_way(s, h) lies within p.off_roadway_reach of x's body (st.region_geometry distance), and no other halted road user occupying s has rel.longitudinal_overlap with x that is not negative.

narrowings.why: 'no person' is read through the vehicle's conduct: a vehicle halted on the road is judged whoever or whatever controls it.

The purposes that tell parking and standing from stopping (loading, receiving passengers) are not observable; every halt is read, and the halts the stopping definition excepts (to avoid conflict, or in compliance with an officer or a device) are not read as stopping, parking or leaving the vehicle standing.

Practicability is read only through a shoulder of the same highway beside the vehicle and free alongside it; other places off the roadway (a turnout, a verge without a mapped shoulder) and the shoulder's surface and width are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a rural highway, asm.business_or_residence_district declared false and both disabled assumptions declared false, a car halts in the right lane for a minute; a free shoulder lies beside it within the reach; no other road user and no device is present.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same halt on a highway with no shoulder within the reach of the car's body.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The same halt with asm.business_or_residence_district declared true.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The forbid scene with no speed observed, so whether the car is halted is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car halts in the lane behind a stopped truck within the queue standstill gap, with a free shoulder beside it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car halts in the lane with asm.vehicle_disabled and asm.disabled_vehicle_immovable declared true.

param_proposals.name: p.queue_standstill_gap
param_proposals.convention: Standstill gap of queued vehicles: the clearance between a vehicle halted in a queue and the one ahead of it; car-following models put the jam gap at about 2 m and observed queues at signals reach about 4 m.
param_proposals.source: Intelligent Driver Model jam distance (Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing 2000) and field observations of standstill spacing at signalized intersections.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique and time-to-collision studies (Hayward 1972; Hyden 1987).

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict.
param_proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique; passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO).

param_proposals.name: p.off_roadway_reach
param_proposals.convention: One standard lane width (12 ft): a shoulder separated from the vehicle's body by no more than one lane is reachable by one lateral move, and is beside the vehicle.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (standard 12 ft travel lane).

residues.why: Attended or unattended, the duty is the same: the words name both cases and exclude neither.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle occupying a highway h and the roadway rw lying on it (st.roadway, st.on_way(rw, h)); asm.business_or_residence_district is false; x is halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance); and not the exception: not (asm.vehicle_disabled and x occupies a roadway and asm.disabled_vehicle_immovable).
obligation: Some st.lane l with st.on_way(l, h) is not occupied by x, has st.lane_width at least p.free_passage_width, and is occupied alongside x (rel.longitudinal_overlap with x not negative) by no other road user that is halted (drv.motion.stopped). Violated where no such lane is left opposite the standing vehicle.

narrowings.why: The unobstructed width is read as a whole lane of the same highway left beside the standing vehicle, free of other halted road users alongside it; width left in part of a lane, and obstruction by objects other than road users, are not read.

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle,
whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event an unobstructed width of the highway opposite a standing vehicle shall be left
for the free passage of other vehicles
and a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.
This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled
while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway
in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: Upon any highway: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.highway, as the mapping index maps 'upon any highway'.
'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the subject's class.

The paved or main-traveled part is the st.roadway ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder') on the highway (st.on_way), which x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies): 'such stopped vehicles' are the vehicles halted upon that part.

Such stopped vehicles are x halted (drv.motion.stopped) upon the roadway. A clear view of them from a distance is st.sight_distance at x's place: 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it, whether or not any road user is there'. Not a stand-in for whether an actual road user saw x (rel.visible): the words require the view to be available, not that anyone looked. The figure is the law's literal.
While on the paved or main-traveled portion: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the st.roadway at the observation.

assumptions.meaning: The stretch of highway at the observation lies within territory classed as a business district or as a residence district.
The road user's vehicle cannot be moved from the place where it stands at the observation, by its own power or otherwise.

residues.why: Attended or unattended, the duty is the same: the words name both cases and exclude neither.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle occupying a highway h and the roadway rw lying on it (st.roadway, st.on_way(rw, h)); asm.business_or_residence_district is false; x is halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance); and not the exception: not (asm.vehicle_disabled and x occupies a roadway and asm.disabled_vehicle_immovable).
obligation: st.sight_distance at x's place is at least the literal 200 ft. Violated where x stands upon the roadway at a place whose sight distance is shorter.

narrowings.why: 'in each direction' is read through the sight distance the source records for the place, which covers the view of approaching traffic and the place's being seen by drivers approaching it; a source that records one figure for the place records the governing (smaller) one.

segmentation.text: A person shall not stop, stand or park
a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic
or in compliance with law
or the directions of a police officer
or official traffic-control device,
in any of the following places:
Within an intersection.

elements.justification: Stop, when prohibited, is DEF-NRS-484A-260 ('any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not'); stand is DEF-NRS-484A-250 ('the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of ... receiving or discharging passengers'); park is DEF-NRS-484A-155 ('the standing of a vehicle ... otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of ... loading or unloading'). Each is a halt: drv.motion.stopped (kin.speed at or below its resolution). The stopping definition's exclusions (conflict, officer, device) are the section's own exceptions, which spans c3 to c6 carry. 'A person' is read through the vehicle's conduct.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), the subject's class.

Other traffic is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway'), other than x. A halt is necessary to avoid conflict with it where a member is in a predicted conflict with x (prim.closest_approach_within over the conflict horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below the conflict clearance), as the mapping index maps '(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;', or where a member stands ahead of x (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame', its longitudinal component positive) within the queue standstill gap of x's body (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies'), so that x cannot proceed without striking it.

The directions of a police officer are a dev.human_direction of role police_officer ('a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}; indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}') with indication stop, governing (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies), as the mapping index maps '(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;' to dev.governs, dev.human_direction, st.travel_region.

An official traffic-control device (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority ... for the purpose of regulating ... traffic') directing a halt is a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, a dev.stop_sign or a dev.yield_sign, governing (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies); its official status is presumed from its presence.

Within an intersection: x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'; DEF-NRS-484A-105, 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines'), as the mapping index maps 'within an intersection'. Not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, which lie outside it.

assumptions.meaning: The road user is required to be halted where it is at the observation by a legal duty other than the direction of an officer or a traffic-control device.

applicability: x is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle whose footprint overlaps an intersection i (rel.occupies(x, i), st.intersection) at the judged observation.
obligation: Violated where x is halted (drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance) and none of the exceptions holds: (c3) some member z of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than x is in a predicted conflict with x (prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_time_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance) or stands ahead of x (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive) with rel.surface_gap below p.queue_standstill_gap; (c4) asm.halt_required_by_law; (c5) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop governs a travel region x occupies or i; (c6) a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, a dev.stop_sign or a dev.yield_sign governs a travel region x occupies or i.

narrowings.why: 'A person' is read through the vehicle's conduct: a vehicle halted in the intersection is judged whoever or whatever controls it.
The purposes that tell standing and parking from stopping (receiving passengers, loading) are not observable; every halt is read, as each of the three words forbids a halt.

scenarios.name: branch_2

param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of tracked road users.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique and time-to-collision studies (Hayward 1972; Hyden 1987).

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict.
param_proposals.source: Traffic-conflict technique; passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO).

param_proposals.name: p.queue_standstill_gap
param_proposals.convention: Standstill gap of queued vehicles: the clearance between a vehicle halted in a queue and the one ahead of it; car-following models put the jam gap at about 2 m and observed queues at signals reach about 4 m.
param_proposals.source: Intelligent Driver Model jam distance (Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing 2000) and field observations of standstill spacing at signalized intersections.

contract: The signed departure of a road user's heading from a carrier's designated direction of travel at the observation, left positive: the sine of the angle from the carrier's direction (st.lane_direction) to the road user's heading (kin.heading), computed as the cross product of the two normalised vectors, the direction's first component times the heading's second minus the direction's second component times the heading's first. A ratio between -1 and 1 up to the normalisation factor both atoms carry; positive where the heading points to the left of the direction, negative where it points to the right, zero where it is aligned with or exactly opposed to it. Not denoted: occupancy of the carrier, which the caller states; whether the road user points with or against the direction, since a heading and its mirror across the perpendicular give the same value, which the caller states where it matters; the direction of motion, since the concept reads where the road user points, not where it moves; a carrier with no designated direction, for which the value is unknown.

elements.justification: kin.heading: 'direction the body points', read normalised; the concept reads where the road user points, as its contract states.
st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in', read normalised; a centre turn lane or uncovered place carries none, and the value is then unknown.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle in a lane whose direction is +x points ten degrees to the left of it; the instance bounds the value between 0.15 and 0.2 and it lies there.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle points along the lane direction; the value is zero, outside the instance's bounds 0.15 to 0.2.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source does not observe the lane's designated direction.

contract: Road user a is overtaking road user b at the observation: the two head the same way (rel.same_direction with cosine tolerance `cos_tol`), their footprints overlap along a's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap not negative, so the two are side by side), and a's speed (kin.speed) exceeds b's by more than `speed_tol`, a tolerance that names only the source's speed resolution. It holds at each observation of the side-by-side phase in which a gains on b, on whichever side of b a is. Not denoted: the approach from behind before the footprints overlap, or the moment a draws clear ahead; the side on which a passes, which the caller states where it matters; b gaining on a; where either road user is, which the caller states.

params.name: cos_tol
params.meaning: cosine of the largest angle between the two headings still read as the same way

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: speed resolution of the source, below which a speed difference counts as none

elements.span: the two head the same way (rel.same_direction with cosine tolerance `cos_tol`)
elements.justification: rel.same_direction: 'headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance'.

elements.span: their footprints overlap along a's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap not negative
elements.justification: rel.longitudinal_overlap: 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side): the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share, negative for the gap between the projections'.

elements.span: a's speed (kin.speed) exceeds b's by more than `speed_tol`
elements.justification: kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity'; a gaining on b is a's speed above b's by more than the resolution.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle at 6 m/s beside a car at 3 m/s heading the same way, their footprints overlapping along the bicycle's heading.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The bicycle at 6 m/s is 10 m behind the car at 3 m/s: the projections do not overlap.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Side by side, but the source supplies no speeds.

contract: A road user has turned to the left through a region, such as an intersection the caller passes: at the observation it leaves the region (its footprint overlaps the region, rel.occupies, at the observation before and not at this one), and its heading change since its entry, integrated from its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate, left positive) with sampling step bound `step`, is at least `min_angle` and below `max_angle`, the band in which the crossing counts as a left turn rather than a through movement or a reversal. The act begins at the entry, the observation at which the overlap last became true. The act is recognized at the observation it leaves the region. The concept holds only at the exit observation, ending at the next observation. Conduct before the entry is not read. Not denoted: a through movement or a heading change to the left below `min_angle`; a turn to the right; a reversal, a change at or beyond `max_angle`; a road user still within the region; which carrier it entered from, which the caller states; a crossing whose entry the recording does not show, for which the heading change since entry is unknown.

params.name: step
params.meaning: sampling step bound of the heading-change integration

params.name: min_angle
params.meaning: heading change to the left from which a crossing is a turn rather than a through movement

params.name: max_angle
params.meaning: heading change at which the heading has come round to the opposite direction, a reversal rather than a turn

act.onset: The act begins at the entry, the observation at which the overlap last became true.
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation it leaves the region.
act.extent: The concept holds only at the exit observation, ending at the next observation.
act.history: Conduct before the entry is not read.

elements.span: its footprint overlaps the region, rel.occupies
elements.justification: rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; the entry and the exit are its rise and its fall.

elements.span: integrated from its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate, left positive)
elements.justification: kin.yaw_rate: 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left (counter-clockwise)'; integrated by the formula language's heading change since the entry, not a stand-in for road curvature.
